record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: Are sub-ion-scale field polarizations in kinetic plasma turbulence genuinely kinetic-Alfven-wave-like, or do the observed spectral ratios instead require a mixture of KAW-like fluctuations, other wave-like modes such as whistler, ion-cyclotron, or ion Bernstein fluctuations, and nonlinear effects that make the turbulence deviate from asymptotic linear KAW predictions? The question is specifically motivated by spectral ratios that are broadly consistent with KAW expectations but do not exactly match the linear-theory values.

evidence.quote: So are the sub-ion-scale field polarizations indeed KAW-like?

sub-ion-scale turbulence can in principle include contributions from wave-like fluctuations of other nature. This may include fluctuations consistent with whistler ... ion-cyclotron ... or ion Bernstein waves
the spectral ratios could also deviate from linear KAW predictions as a result of nonlinear dynamics

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a magnetized, weakly collisional plasma exhibiting a turbulent cascade that extends below the ion gyroradius and ion inertial scales (the "sub-ion" range). At these scales, linear Vlasov–Maxwell theory admits several wave branches, including:

(i) kinetic Alfvén waves (KAW), characterized by predicted ratios among electric, magnetic, density, and velocity fluctuations,
(ii) whistler waves,
(iii) ion-cyclotron waves, and
(iv) ion Bernstein waves.

For each linear branch one can compute predicted "spectral ratios" — e.g. the ratio of magnetic compressibility |δB_∥|²/|δB|², the density-magnetic ratio (n_e/n_0)²/(δB_∥/B_0)², and the Alfvén ratio |δu|²/|δB|² in appropriate units — as functions of the perpendicular wavenumber k_⊥ρ_i.

Suppose that in fully kinetic 3D-3V simulations (and in spacecraft observations) of sub-ion-range turbulence the measured spectral ratios are broadly close to the linear KAW predictions but do not match them exactly.

Question. Determine whether the sub-ion-scale electromagnetic and density polarizations of the turbulent fluctuations are genuinely dominated by KAW-like modes, or whether the observed deviations from linear KAW spectral ratios are produced by:
(a) an admixture of other linear wave branches (whistler, ion-cyclotron, and/or ion-Bernstein fluctuations) coexisting with KAWs in the cascade, and/or
(b) intrinsically nonlinear dynamics that drive the polarizations away from any asymptotic linear-mode prediction.

Quantify the relative contributions of (a) and (b) and identify a diagnostic, computable from the field correlation tensor of the turbulence, that unambiguously distinguishes a single-mode KAW cascade from a multi-mode and/or strongly nonlinear sub-ion cascade producing the same approximate spectral ratios.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2020–2024) continues to debate the nature of sub-ion-scale fluctuations. A 2020 Phys. Rev. Research paper argues for coexistence of KAW and ion Bernstein modes in solar-wind sub-ion compressive turbulence, while a 2024 Frontiers article presents simulations showing that even cascades initialized with whistlers evolve toward KAW-like polarizations, but with non-negligible non-KAW power. Spacecraft (MMS) measurements of Alfvén ratios likewise show approximate but imperfect agreement with linear KAW predictions. No consensus has been reached on disentangling the relative contributions of mode mixing versus nonlinear effects, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Possible coexistence of kinetic Alfvén and ion Bernstein modes in sub-ion scale compressive turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: non-negligible component of power ... may be ion Bernstein modes
status_evidence.claim: Mode coexistence (KAW + ion Bernstein) is supported in solar-wind sub-ion turbulence.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic Alfvén wave cascade in sub-ion range plasma turbulence (Frontiers, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: observed polarization relations at later times match better with the KAW relations compared to whistlers
status_evidence.claim: Cascades preferentially develop KAW-like polarizations, but deviations remain.

status_evidence.title: Ion-Scale Kinetic Alfvén Turbulence: MMS Measurements of the Alfvén Ratio
status_evidence.snippet: spectral field ratios ... measure wave-like polarization properties as compared to linear theory
status_evidence.claim: Observations show approximate but imperfect agreement with linear KAW spectral ratios.
